title: The American Civil War - OverSimplified (Part 1)
beats: Lincoln's birth parody, then his childhood and lawyer moon-almanac story
Founding vague promises: 'what does that mean exactly' repeated; cannonball joke
North/South split by economy: industry versus plantation cotton
Missouri script: 11 free and 11 slave states balanced; compromise declared 'solved forever'
'A few years later it came up again', then explains why balance matters
California script replays the Missouri template; Compromise of 1850
Kansas-Nebraska, popular choice, Bleeding Kansas, John Brown
Uncle Tom's Cabin, Republican party, Sumner caning, Dred Scott
'Let's strip all of that away': slavery as the human reality of 4 million people
Northern opposition often economic; Lincoln's position moral but cautious
John Brown at Harpers Ferry, 'a million John Browns' joke
Lincoln's 1860 win, secession, states' documents quoted about slavery
Lincoln beard and inauguration, Fort Sumter
Both sides expect quick war: 'is it over yet?'; population gap
Anaconda plan stated in three prongs after joke strategy meeting
Bull Run: picnickers, Stonewall nickname; Wilmer McLean flees
Lincoln's depth: folksy but shrewd, wartime controversies
Grant and Fort Donelson nickname, Shiloh
McLean flees war again at second Bull Run
Britain and cotton; why Lincoln needs a victory before emancipation
Lost orders around cigars, Antietam, McClellan fired
Emancipation Proclamation reframes the war as about a union without slavery

theory: The video teaches the cause of the war by acting the same compromise script twice with different states, so the viewer discovers the rule that expansion breaks the balance. It then deliberately switches tone at 8:08 to say what the politics meant for people, and uses sources to remove doubt about motive. Comic form carries structure; seriousness is used sparingly and flagged.
velocity: Scene builder: replay an identical scripted scene with a new entity to expose the template
Voice: allow an explicitly announced tonal shift when the stakes change
Orchestrator: use a recurring minor character as a visible counter of repetition
Learner model: offer a primary source quote when the learner doubts motive
Evals: after the second replay, ask the learner to predict the third state's outcome
